We got many templates. Need to find one that matches our target molecule. The first entry seems to have retro_smarts_template that includes [#7;a:8]:[c:7](-[NH2...]) etc. That seems like an amine attached to aromatic heterocycle. Our target molecule: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. It has an anilide attached to a triazine? Actually c2nnn(... )c2N is a triazine ring with an amine substituent. The amine is attached to aromatic ring via NH-CO-? Wait structure: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. So there is an aniline (aryl amine) attached to carbonyl linking to triazine. The triazine has a side chain Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 (aryl with a tertiary amine). The SN2 step likely is the formation of the C-N bond between the aryl carbon (maybe the side chain) and the N of the azetidine? Actually SN2 typical on alkyl halide, not aryl. The side chain includes CN4CC(F)C4 which is a tertiary amine attached via CH2 to aromatic ring. That could be formed via SN2 of a halide (e.g., aryl chloride) with N of azetidine? But aryl SN2 is not typical. Maybe the SN2 is on the side chain: the carbon attached to aromatic ring (benzylic) is attached to N4CC(F)C4 via CH2. So the SN2 could be substitution of a halide (e.g., benzylic chloride) by the tertiary amine (N4...). So retrosynthesis: break C-N bond between benzylic carbon and N of azetidine, replace with C-Cl (halide). So we need a template that breaks C-N (alkyl amine) and forms halide.

Search for templates where forward forms halide? Actually forward forms C-N, breaks halide. So we need functional_groups_broken = ["halide"] and functional_groups_formed = ["primary amines","secondary amines","tertiary amines"] maybe. Our search returned many templates, but we need to test which matches our molecule.

We can iterate through returned templates and use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching to see if the retro_smarts_template matches our molecule. The tool expects template_id (string). The result entries have template_hash but also reaction_id. The template_id likely is reaction_id? Or template_hash? The tool expects template_id (string) referencing template in database. Probably use reaction_id as template_id. Let's test first entry reaction_id 1014069.


<thought>Check if template 1014069 matches our molecule.</thought>
<action>check_smiles_reaction_template_matching</action>
<action_input>{
    "smiles": "COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1",
    "template_id": "1014069"
}</action_input>
